verdict.rationale: Zep documents first-party deletion controls. Deleting a User cascades to all Threads and thread artifacts in one API call, aimed at Right To Be Forgotten requests, and nodes and edges can be deleted individually, with node deletion also removing connected edges. Nothing in the evidence describes configurable retention periods or automatic expiry, so only the deletion half of the story is covered. missing for 10: configurable data retention policies/TTLs, automatic expiry of threads or graph data, independent or hands-on corroboration of deletion behavior

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: Deleting a User will delete all Threads and thread artifacts associated with that User with a single API call, making it easy to handle Right To Be Forgotten requests.
This single-operation approach makes it simple to handle Right To Be Forgotten (RTBF) requests and comply with privacy regulations.
Deleting a node will also delete all edges connected to that node.
